segments.arabic: [946] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع وعبد الله بن دينار عن ابن عمر
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘ and ‘Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا سأل رسول الله ﷺ عن صلاة الليل، فقال رسول الله عليه السلام صلاة الليل مثنى مثنى فإذا خشي أحدكم الصبح صلى ركعة واحدة توتر له ما قد صلى
segments.english: A man asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about the night prayer. The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, said, “The night prayer is two units at a time. If one of you fears the coming of morning, he prays one unit, making what he has prayed odd in number.”

segments.arabic: وعن نافع
segments.english: And from Nafi‘:

segments.arabic: أن عبد الله بن عمر كان يسلم بين الركعة والركعتين في الوتر حتى يأمر ببعض حاجته
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar used to give the closing greeting between the single unit and the two units of Witr, even giving instructions about some need of his.

notes: Both complete portions of the selected report are retained, including the second Nafi‘ route and Ibn ‘Umar’s intervening instructions. Dar Ibn Kathir prints them separately as 990 and 991; the single selected reference 946 remains intact. No occurrence has been removed or a new app number invented.

The source has ﷺ in the question and the shorter عليه السلام in the answer. Their English forms remain distinct. Brill uses Prophet in the first designation and the longer honorific in the answer; the selected source is unchanged.
The single-unit/two-unit order in بين الركعة والركعتين is retained. Neither an obligatory classification nor an extra timing instruction is supplied.

segments.arabic: [947] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن مخرمة بن سليمان عن كريب ان ابن عباس أخبره
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, that Ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

segments.arabic: أنه بات عند ميمونة وهي خالته فاضطجعت في عرض وسادة واضطجع رسول الله ﷺ وأهله في طولها فنام حتى انتصف الليل أو قريبا منه فاستيقظ يمسح النوم عن وجهه ثم قرأ عشر آيات من آل عمران ثم قام رسول الله ﷺ إلى شن معلقة فتوضأ فأحسن الوضوء ثم قام يصلي فصنعت مثله فقمت إلى جنبه فوضع يده اليمنى على رأسي وأخذ بأذني يفتلها ثم صلى ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم ركعتين ثم أوتر ثم اضطجع حتى جاءه المؤذن فقام فصلى ركعتين ثم خرج فصلى الصبح
segments.english: He spent the night with Maymunah, who was his maternal aunt. I lay across the width of a pillow, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. He slept until midnight, or close to it. Then he awoke, wiping sleep from his face, and recited ten verses from Al ‘Imran. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to an old waterskin that was hanging and performed ablution well. Then he stood to pray. I did as he had done and stood beside him. He placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my ear, twisting it. Then he prayed two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units. Then he prayed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two units, then went out and prayed the morning prayer.

notes: All six repeated pairs before Witr are retained individually, as in both inspected Arabic prints. The pinned Khan-family comparison 2.16.106 says five times; that count is not substituted into the translation. Its editorial cross-reference is not part of the selected narration.

The source changes from third-person introduction to first-person account; both are retained. Pillow follows وسادة; bed in the Bewley comparison does not replace it. The source says ten verses, without supplying last.

Both source honorifics, midnight uncertainty, the worn hanging waterskin, right hand, ear-twisting, both later pairs of units and final morning prayer remain. Brill expands Malik to Malik ibn Anas and uses a definite form of pillow; neither change is imported.

segments.arabic: [948] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان قال: حدثني ابن وهب قال: أخبرني عمرو أن عبد الرحمن بن القاسم حدثه عن أبيه عن عبد الله بن عمر قال:
segments.english: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to me. He said: ‘Amr informed me that ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim related to him, from his father, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar. He said:

segments.arabic: قال النبي ﷺ صلاة الليل مثنى مثنى فإذا أردت أن تنصرف فاركع ركعة توتر لك ما صليت
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “The night prayer is two units at a time. When you wish to finish, pray one unit, making what you have prayed odd in number.”

segments.arabic: قال القاسم ورأينا أناسا منذ أدركنا يوترون بثلاث وإن كلا لواسع أرجو أن لا يكون بشيء منه بأس
segments.english: Al-Qasim said: Since we reached maturity, we have seen people praying Witr with three units. There is latitude in either way. I hope there is nothing wrong with any of it.

notes: The complete chain retains Ibn Wahb and ‘Amr without importing their expanded names from Brill. All singular and plural transmission verbs remain distinct.
Al-Qasim’s closing comment is separately identified as transmission material, not words of the Prophet. No consecutive/continuous qualification is added to the three units.
The provisional maturity rendering and latitude wording were checked against al-‘Ayni’s lexical discussion. His legal discussion is not inserted into the report or turned into app advice.

segments.arabic: [949] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري عن عروة أن عائشة أخبرته
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, that ‘A’ishah informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يصلي إحدى عشرة ركعة كانت تلك صلاته
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray eleven units. That was his prayer.

segments.arabic: تعني بالليل
segments.english: She means at night.

segments.arabic: فيسجد السجدة من ذلك قدر ما يقرأ أحدكم خمسين آية قبل أن يرفع رأسه ويركع ركعتين قبل صلاة الفجر ثم يضطجع على شقه الأيمن حتى يأتيه المؤذن للصلاة
segments.english: In that prayer, he would remain in a prostration for as long as it takes one of you to recite fifty verses before raising his head. He would pray two units before the dawn prayer, then lie on his right side until the caller to prayer came to him for the prayer.

notes: The feminine source gloss تعني بالليل is retained separately as She means at night, without assigning an additional named speaker. It is not silently absorbed into a quotation from the Prophet.
Eleven units, fifty verses, raising the head, two units before dawn, the right side and the caller’s arrival all remain. No Sunna/compulsory parenthetical is borrowed from the English comparisons.
Brill has a direct transmission verb before ‘Urwah and a masculine means gloss; the selected عن and تعني are unchanged.

segments.arabic: [950] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد قال: حدثنا أنس بن سيرين قال:
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us. He said: Anas ibn Sirin related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: قلت لابن عمر أرأيت الركعتين قبل صلاة الغداة أطيل فيهما القراءة، فقال: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي من الليل مثنى مثنى ويوتر بركعة ويصلي الركعتين قبل صلاة الغداة وكأن الأذان بأذنيه
segments.english: I said to Ibn ‘Umar, “Tell me about the two units before the morning prayer: should I prolong the recitation in them?” He said, “The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray at night two units at a time and pray Witr with one unit. He would pray the two units before the morning prayer as though the call to prayer were in his ears.”

segments.arabic: قال حماد أي سرعة
segments.english: Hammad said: Meaning, quickly.

notes: The question about lengthening recitation, the two-at-a-time night prayer, one-unit Witr and the image of the call being in his ears remain. Hammad’s speed gloss is separate transmission material.
The source names Anas ibn Sirin, not Anas ibn Malik. No additional call, congregation timing or ruling is supplied.

segments.arabic: [951] حدثنا عمر بن حفص قال: حدثنا أبي قال: حدثنا الأعمش قال: حدثني مسلم عن مسروق عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: ‘Umar ibn Hafs related to us. He said: My father related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us. He said: Muslim related to me, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

segments.arabic: كل الليل أوتر رسول الله ﷺ وانتهى وتره إلى السحر
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed Witr at every part of the night, and his Witr eventually came to be at the time before dawn.

notes: Every part of the night renders the temporal كل الليل; it does not mean a whole night continuously spent in Witr or simply every night. Ibn Hajar’s discussion identifies the expression as time within the night.
The ending at the time before dawn remains. No Isha parenthesis, first/middle/last enumeration, illness, travel or until-death phrase is imported from other versions or commentary.

segments.arabic: [952] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى قال: حدثنا هشام قال: حدثني أبي عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: My father related to me, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي وأنا راقدة معترضة على فراشه فإذا أراد أن يوتر أيقظني فأوترت
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while I lay asleep across his bed. When he wanted to pray Witr, he would wake me, and I would pray Witr.

notes: The selected unexpanded names Yahya and Hisham and the singular my father related to me remain. No honorific absent from the selected ‘A’ishah introduction is added from Brill.
Sleeping across the bed, his intention to pray Witr, awakening her and her own Witr all remain.

segments.arabic: [953] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى بن سعيد عن عبيد الله حدثني نافع عن عبد الله عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya ibn Sa‘id related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah: Nafi‘ related to me, from ‘Abdullah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said:

segments.arabic: اجعلوا آخر صلاتكم بالليل وترا
segments.english: “Make Witr your last prayer at night.”

segments.arabic: [954] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن أبي بكر ابن عمر بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب عن سعيد بن يسار أنه قال:
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, from Sa‘id ibn Yasar, that he said:

segments.arabic: كنت أسير مع عبد الله بن عمر بطريق مكة، فقال سعيد فلما خشيت الصبح نزلت فأوترت ثم لحقته، فقال عبد الله بن عمر أين كنت فقلت: خشيت الصبح فنزلت فأوترت، فقال عبد الله أليس لك في رسول الله ﷺ أسوة حسنة فقلت: بلى والله قال: فإن رسول الله ﷺ كان يوتر على البعير
segments.english: I was travelling with ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar on the road to Makkah. Sa‘id said: When I feared the coming of morning, I dismounted and prayed Witr, then caught up with him. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said, “Where were you?” I said, “I feared the coming of morning, so I dismounted and prayed Witr.” ‘Abdullah said, “Do you not have a good example in the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” I said, “Yes, by Allah.” He said, “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Witr on the camel.”

notes: The full Abu Bakr genealogy, Sa‘id’s self-attribution, both dismounting statements and the entire exchange remain. No route name is substituted for the road to Makkah.
Both Messenger honorifics and the oath are retained. No inference about obligatory prayers or a general legal rule is appended.

segments.arabic: [955] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا جويرية بن أسماء عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال:
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Juwayriyah ibn Asma’ related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي في السفر على راحلته حيث توجهت به يومئ إيماء صلاة الليل إلا الفرائض ويوتر على راحلته
segments.english: When travelling, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the night prayer on his mount, making gestures, whichever way it turned with him, except for the obligatory prayers. He would pray Witr on his mount.

notes: The night-prayer limitation, whichever direction the mount takes, gestures, exception for obligatory prayers and Witr on the mount remain. No bowing/prostration detail absent from this source is supplied.

segments.arabic: [956] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن محمد قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad. He said:

segments.arabic: وسئل أنس أقنت النبي ﷺ في الصبح قال: نعم فقيل له أو قنت قبل الركوع قال بعد الركوع يسيرا
segments.english: Anas was asked, “Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, perform qunut in the morning prayer?” He said, “Yes.” He was asked, “Did he perform qunut before bowing?” He said, “After bowing, for a short time.”

notes: The source names Muhammad and Anas without the fuller names in Brill. Both questions and answers and the before/after distinction remain.
A short time renders يسيرا without inserting the precise month from the next report or the Khan-family parenthesis. The pending next report is not required to read this complete occurrence.

segments.arabic: [958] أخبرنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا زائدة عن التيمي عن أبي مجلز عن أنس قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus informed us. He said: Za’idah related to us, from al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, from Anas. He said:

segments.arabic: قنت النبي ﷺ شهرا يدعو على رعل وذكوان
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, performed qunut for a month, supplicating against Ri‘l and Dhakwan.

notes: The opening informed us preserves أخبرنا; Brill instead prints related to us and expands Anas to Anas ibn Malik. The selected digital wording is unchanged.

segments.arabic: كان القنوت في المغرب والفجر
